newsitem.title: UK: U.S. funds uncertain on Dow direction - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. funds uncertain on Dow direction - survey.

text.p: U.S.-based fund managers are unsure about which way the Dow will go next and are continuing to cut their exposure to domestic equities, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.
It said respondents to the May survey were evenly divided on Dow direction on a three month view, but sellers were outnumbering buyers by a balance of 13 percent.
The last time buyers were in majority in the survey was in December 1995.
U.S. fund managers were less bullish on the prospects for overseas equity markets.
"With valuations looking high, they are unwilling to add further to their Continental European exposure and are net sellers of UK equities," the report said.
The only overseas market seeing significant buying interest in the survey was Japan, where buyers outnumbered sellers by a balance of 30 percent.
The favourite sector in the U.S. was technology, with financials still popular and building cyclicals out of favour.
U.S. funds were increased buyers of domestic bonds but sellers of bonds outside the U.S., it said.
The survey of U.S.-based fund managers was carried out by Gallup on behalf of Merrill between May 2 and 6, covering 47 institutions responsible for funds totalling $1,942 billion.
